title_zh: WebVoyager：基于大型多模态模型构建端到端网页智能体
one_line: GPT-4V agent acts on live websites via Set-of-Mark-labelled element screenshots; human-judged live success beats text-only and GPT-4 All Tools; GPT-4V evaluator validated against humans.
one_line_zh: 用带数字标注的网页截图让GPT-4V在真实网站上端到端操作，人工评估在线成功率优于纯文本基线，并验证GPT-4V自动评估器。

online_eval.quote: we do not host any websites locally and allow the agent to explore the open web instead, which poses unique challenges such as floating ads, pop-up windows, constant updates, etc.

held_out_env.quote: We also evaluate WebVoyager on 90 web-related tasks of level 1 and level 2 from the GAIA ( Mialon et al., 2023 ) , and 50 interactive open-web tasks from SeeAct Zheng et al. (2024) .

strong_baselines.quote: We compare our WebVoyager with 1) GPT-4 (All Tools) , and 2) WebVoyager in a text-only setting which employs the textual accessibility tree proposed in WebArena ( Zhou et al., 2023 ) to describe web pages.

budget_matched.quote: We set the temperature to 1 during generation and allow the agent to explore at most 15 steps.

component_ablation.quote: WebVoyager achieves a Task Success Rate of 59.1% on our new benchmark, significantly outperforming GPT-4 (All Tools) with a rate of 30.8% and the text-only setting with a rate of 40.1%

validator_check.quote: GPT-4V’s agreement with human annotators gradually improves as it receives more information, and its final Kappa score also reaches 0.7, which is on par with the agreement among human annotators.

evidence_level.quote: we save screenshots throughout the online navigation process and then use GPT-4V to evaluate these trajectories together with the final results automatically. Human evaluations are also conducted to verify the results

S2.quote: We also provide the agent with auxiliary text as inputs, including the textual content embedded within the interactive element, the type of the element, and possibly some comment text in the aria-label attribute.

S4.quote: We develop an automated web-browsing environment using Selenium .

S5.quote: As illustrated in Figure 2 , the nature of webpages allows us to locate and outline each interactive element using this tool precisely.

F5.quote: First, we haven’t supported all possible actions in our environment compared to actions a human user might take when browsing the web. e.g. the Drag action on web pages. Supporting such an action is challenging since the degree of Drag is not a finite set.

AP4.quote: We report the Agreement (the ratio of overlap) and Kappa ( ; Cohen 1960 ) between consolidated human labels and GPT-4V’s judgments on the subset of 300 tasks in Table 2 .

AP8.quote: Tasks related to real-time information, where the answer might change, e.g., flight ticket prices. Hence, the “Possible” answers were also correct during our experiments.

AP12.quote: We may allow it to choose the pixel values to be dragged if the Visual Grounding capabilities of LMMs are further enhanced.
